rows.notes: The study is a desk-based review of CSR literature, climate-finance literature and the public CSR reports of five coffee companies (Tim Hortons, Dunkin', Tchibo, Starbucks, Nestl<U+00E9>); it collects no field, survey, experimental or model data of its own and is best classed as a review/essay. Even if the document analysis were counted as primary, the paper never mentions drip, sensor-based or efficient irrigation; the only irrigation-adjacent wording is a generic listing of 'improved soil and water management' and 'improving water collection and management' among adaptation options, drawn from cited sources (Cohn et al. 2017, Davis et al. 2012, Laderach et al. 2017), not from any result of its own. It provides no evidence that drip or sensor-based irrigation delivers drought risk management for coffee.

notes: Full text appears complete (13 pages, including references). The paper is a conceptual/CSR analysis of coffee companies and is unrelated to irrigation technology performance; its citation for drip/sensor-based irrigation as a drought-adaptation measure is not supported by any content in the article.
